result.why_top_candidate_wins: signal_chile_flu has the highest composite score (7) and the strongest direct support for explaining the missed US hospitalization peak. The support subgraph shows a direct LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR relationship to the target signal (signal_us_hosp) (+3) and two distinct links to the mechanism (IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF, +2 each). In contrast, the next-best candidate (Australia) lacks an IMPORTATION_LINK to the US mechanism (score 5), and the travel-pressure candidate lacks a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR edge to the target (score 4). Thus Chile activity uniquely combines a predictive relationship to the observed hospital signal and mechanistic links into the US mechanism, making it the most plausible single hidden driver given the provided evidence and ranking.
result.proposed_minimal_edit: Add an importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base: create/activate an edge signal_chile_flu --> eq_us_flu_base labeled IMPORTATION_INFLUX (time-lagged), and expose one coupling parameter (e.g., beta_chile_import) to be estimated. This is a minimal mechanistic edit that operationalizes the existing IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF edges in the support subgraph.
result.caveat: The support is based on graph relationships and ranking, not causal proof. Shared seasonality or common external drivers could produce the observed LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR link; estimated coupling and lag must be tested for significance and robustness before concluding causality. Other candidates (e.g., travel pressure, Australia) may still contribute and/or interact with Chile signals.
